questions.text: What is meant by wave interference?
answers: the bending of waves incident on an obstacle or a slit whose dimensions are of the order of the wavelength into the region behind the obstacle.
the increase or decrease of the amplitude of the resulting wave when two coherent waves are superposed.
the reflection of waves from an obstacle at some angle and their propagation back.
the sharp increase or decrease of the amplitude of the resulting oscillations as a result of the superposition of two waves.

questions.text: When is wave interference observed?
answers: when waves with different frequencies and phase difference are superposed.
when waves with the same frequency and a varying phase difference are superposed.
when waves with different frequencies and a constant phase difference are superposed.
when waves with constant frequencies and phase difference are superposed.
when waves with the same frequency and a constant phase difference are superposed.

questions.text: Under what condition do waves of different wavelengths interfere?
answers: when their amplitudes are the same.
when their amplitudes and initial phases are the same.
when their initial phases are the same.

Which waves are called coherent?
answers: with the same frequency and a constant phase difference.

questions.text: Choose the correct statement.
answers: light waves with the same frequency and a constant phase difference are called mutually coherent waves.
light sources with the same frequency are called mutually coherent sources.
waves with the same wavelength polarized in the same plane are called coherent waves.
waves with the same amplitude and wavelength polarized in mutually perpendicular planes are called mutually coherent waves.
it is impossible to ensure mutual coherence of light waves from a natural source.

answers: $M$ is a minimum, $N$ is a maximum.

questions.text: The increase of intensity in some places and its decrease in others as a result of the superposition of two light waves is called ... .
Is interference observed when two light beams with different wavelengths are superposed, and if so, what condition must be satisfied?
answers: the initial phases must be the same.
the oscillation amplitudes and initial phases must be the same.
the path difference must remain constant.
the oscillation amplitudes must be the same.

questions.text: Under what condition can interference be observed for two light beams of different wavelengths?
answers: with oscillations of the same amplitude.
with oscillations of the same initial phase.
with oscillations of the same initial phase and amplitude.

Why is no interference of light observed from two independent light sources (for example, two stars)?
